concepts.heading: Relationship Orientation as Identity
concepts.alt: A guide holding a compass whose needle is a heart
concepts.plain: For many people, how they do relationships is part of who they are.

concepts.heading: The Full Spectrum
concepts.alt: Spread out along a wide curved path, each standing on a different coloured tile
concepts.plain: One partner or several: every setup everyone agrees to is a real choice.

checks.prompt: For many people, their approach to relationships is…
options: A fundamental part of who they are
checks.explanation: A fundamental part of who they are. For many people, their approach to relationships is not simply a lifestyle choice but a fundamental aspect of who they are — a relationship orientation.

checks.prompt: According to the lesson, monogamy is…
checks.explanation: Also a choice. Monogamy remains the most culturally normative relationship structure, but Sheff's research reminds us that it too is a choice, not a default.

b0e9c4d6-18fe-4b84-b957-85883e9debae.takeaway: How many partners you want is part of who you are, and every agreed setup is valid.

concepts.heading: Structural Approaches to Polyamory
concepts.plain: Having several partners can be arranged in different ways.

concepts.heading: Kitchen Table Polyamory
concepts.alt: Four guides sitting around a kitchen table sharing breakfast
concepts.plain: "Kitchen table" means everyone is comfortable hanging out together.

concepts.heading: Parallel Polyamory
concepts.alt: Two guides walking along two separate parallel paths, each looking ahead
concepts.plain: "Parallel" means your partners do not really mix.

concepts.heading: Garden Party Polyamory
concepts.alt: Three guides chatting politely at a garden party with drinks
concepts.plain: "Garden party" means partners are friendly at events but not close.

concepts.heading: Hierarchical and Non-Hierarchical Approaches
concepts.alt: A guide holding a small ladder in one hand and a flat ring in the other
concepts.plain: Some people rank their relationships. Others treat them as equal.

concepts.heading: Common Pitfalls
concepts.alt: A couple stands on a small raised platform while the third stands lower beside it
concepts.plain: Watch for one couple's comfort always coming first.

checks.prompt: All partners and metamours are comfortable sharing a meal together. Which style is this?
checks.explanation: Kitchen table polyamory. Kitchen table polyamory describes a style where all partners and metamours (your partner's partners) are comfortable sitting around a kitchen table together.

checks.prompt: Metamours have little or no direct contact. Which style is this?
checks.explanation: Parallel polyamory. Parallel polyamory is a style where metamours have little or no direct interaction.

b3108975-1ad5-4e7b-b0ee-f9ad1ec5a8a9.takeaway: There are many ways to arrange several relationships. Pick what works for everyone involved.

concepts.heading: Relationship Anarchy: Rejecting Prescribed Hierarchies
concepts.alt: A guide tossing a rulebook over her shoulder and drawing her own star map
concepts.plain: Relationship anarchy means no built-in ranking. Each bond is its own thing.

concepts.heading: Solo Polyamory: Centering Autonomy
concepts.alt: A guide standing confidently in front of his own small house, keys in hand
concepts.plain: Solo polyamory means you stay your own home base while loving others.

concepts.heading: The Intersection of RA and Solo Poly
concepts.plain: The two often go together, because both drop the usual script.

concepts.heading: Chosen Family and Non-Romantic Life Partnerships
concepts.alt: Three guides hugging in a group, a house icon with a heart above them
concepts.plain: Friends and chosen family can matter just as much as romantic partners.

concepts.heading: Unique Challenges
concepts.alt: A guide pushing against a big rubber stamp shaped like a couple icon
concepts.plain: Laws and other people's expectations are built for couples, which makes this harder.

checks.prompt: In solo polyamory, what is a central value?
checks.explanation: Individual autonomy. Solo polyamory is a relationship approach where maintaining individual autonomy is a central value.

checks.after: Chosen Family and Non-Romantic Life Partnerships
checks.prompt: Which relationships do these frameworks lift up that mainstream culture often overlooks?
checks.explanation: Chosen family and non-romantic partnerships. Both frameworks elevate relationships that mainstream culture often undervalues, such as chosen family and non-romantic life partnerships.

4fe1dab9-b79a-4bec-9582-75ad3d642429.takeaway: You can build your relationships your own way and still have deep, lasting bonds.

concepts.heading: Mono-Normativity and Its Effects
concepts.alt: A guide standing under a big signpost that points only one way, looking sceptical
concepts.plain: Many people assume one partner is the only normal way. That hurts everyone else.

concepts.heading: Respecting Monogamy
concepts.alt: A happy couple holding hands under one shared umbrella
concepts.plain: Choosing one partner is just as valid. Do not look down on it.

concepts.heading: Navigating Transitions Between Structures
concepts.alt: A guide crossing a small bridge between two differently coloured lands
concepts.plain: People change. Moving between setups takes time and honest talk.

concepts.heading: Discussing Relationship Orientation
concepts.alt: A guide opening a door a little and peeking out with a letter in her hand
concepts.plain: Telling others how you do relationships is your call, at your pace.

concepts.heading: When Conflicts Arise
concepts.alt: Two guides sitting at a table with two different maps, talking calmly
concepts.plain: If you and a partner want different setups, be honest. Sometimes it cannot be solved.

checks.prompt: The assumption that monogamy is the natural, default and superior way to relate is called…
checks.explanation: Mono-normativity. Mono-normativity — the cultural assumption that monogamy is the natural, default, and superior way to structure relationships — affects everyone, regardless of their relationship orientation.

checks.prompt: Within CNM communities, how should monogamy be treated?
checks.explanation: With respect, not as inferior. Within CNM communities, it's important to guard against the opposite form of judgment — treating monogamy as inferior, unenlightened, or evidence of insecurity.

d4deda34-2719-43fa-9007-dc46c58777bf.takeaway: No consensual relationship style is better than another, including monogamy.
